title: Pilot latency sculpting - weekly sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on TTFT regressions after kernel swap, streaming handshake timeouts during microburst traffic, and sequence-length pathing for amortized latency. Agreed on next experiments for a small-batch microburst test, set of kernel fallbacks, and security doc handoff.
next_steps: Redwood: share kernel-selection spreadsheet and perf traces by 2027-08-17
BlueArc: run microburst synthetic with 1s inter-arrival and share logs by 2027-08-19
Schedule kernel-level profiling session (Owen + Samir) for 2027-08-20
action_items: Maya Chen: send SOC2 / encryption/KMS FAQ link - due 2027-08-16
Owen Patel: upload kernel traces and annotated flamegraphs to shared drive - due 2027-08-17
Samir Bhatt: run microburst experiment and attach logs in ticket - due 2027-08-19
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-14
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (BlueArc Head of Platform), Ethan Ruiz (SRE), Samir Bhatt (ML Eng)

Summary: quick status, dig into the TTFT spike after kernel swap, streaming handshake jitter in bursts, decide next microburst tests and ownership.

[00:00:05] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we have like 50 minutes on this. Quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Priya Nair: Priya here, Ethan here. Samir joining.
[00:00:18] Maya Chen: Great. Owen from my side?
[00:00:20] Owen Patel: Yep Owen on. I'll lead the deep dive on the kernel traces in a bit.
[00:00:28] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: TTFT numbers since last week, streaming handshake and microburst behavior, sequence length gating, then decisions and next steps.

[00:00:45] Priya Nair: Quick context, we swapped to the new int8 kernel last Tuesday because of cost, and TTFT climbed on tail for short queries. We basically saw a 30 to 40 percent bump on sub-150 token requests.
[00:01:05] Ethan Ruiz: Yeah and during production spikes we saw a handful of streaming handshakes failing or timing out, which caused clients to re-open connections and created extra load.

[00:01:20] Owen Patel: Okay so two things there, TTFT and streaming handshake. On the kernel traces we pulled, there's an extra setup path the kernel takes for the quant path on small seqs — the runtime isn't using the fastpath because it misclassifies the prefix as a cold KV cache. There's like a 40ms hit per first token in some cases.
[00:01:45] Samir Bhatt: Misclassifies the cache as cold, like why? We primed the warm pool in staging.
[00:01:51] Owen Patel: Right, could be due to how requests are pinned to pods in your dedicated slice. We saw a pattern where pod churn + our batcher TTL of 2s means subsequent requests hit a different worker. So KV ends up missing. It's a routing + batching TTL interaction.
[00:02:10] Priya Nair: Hmm that matches our infra churn during deploys. We had a canary deployment Tuesday afternoon.

[00:02:25] Maya Chen: For clarity — this is not a model regression, it's operational; but kernel selection made the hit worse. The int8 kernel has a higher overhead for prefix normalization on cold caches.

[00:02:45] Ethan Ruiz: Is there a way to force the fastpath? Even as a temporary toggle?
[00:02:51] Owen Patel: We do have a fastpath flag in the runtime. It's gated behind cache heuristics today. We can expose a conservative override for your pilot while we tune batcher TTLs. It'll force the sequence to use the optimized attention kernels for first tokens, at the expense of slightly riskier memory usage.

[00:03:12] Priya Nair: Ok, acceptable for pilot. We want tight telemetry though so we can revert quickly if it causes other issues.

[00:03:30] Maya Chen: Action: Owen will prepare a kernel override build and a quick install note. Owen, is that a hotfix or config?
[00:03:38] Owen Patel: Config flag + small runtime restart. No full build required for the override. We'll give exact steps in the doc.

[00:03:50] [00:04:05] Maya Chen: Next streaming handshake, Ethan can you describe the client behavior?
[00:04:10] Ethan Ruiz: Clients open long-lived streams but during sudden bursts — like the vectextracts job we run — the handshake completes but the ACK/response is delayed and some clients time out at 2.5 seconds. They then retry, which multiplies the microburst.
[00:04:30] Owen Patel: From our capture the problem looks like queueing in the server's receive path when there's a sudden spike in new streams. The connection acceptance is serialised briefly and that adds latency to the first chunk.

[00:04:50] Samir Bhatt: Could this be helped by connection pre-warming or a small acceptor pool?
[00:04:58] Owen Patel: Exactly. There are two knobs: increase acceptor concurrency and pre-warm a small pool of idle streams. The tradeoff is slightly more memory used for idle streams vs improved TTFT during microbursts.

[00:05:12] Priya Nair: We're okay to accept some memory overhead for now. Pilot is more about meeting SLOs.

[00:05:25] Maya Chen: Good. We'll propose a pre-warm patch and instructions. Owen will own the patch, Ethan will verify against your microburst harness.

[00:05:40] [00:06:00] Owen Patel: On sequence lengths — Samir, you said most of your calls are under 100 tokens, but you also have a long-tail with 1-2% over 1k tokens. That distribution matters because the runtime picks kernels differently for long sequences; amortized latency changes.
[00:06:18] Samir Bhatt: Yes it's roughly 70% < 60 tokens, 25% 60-300, 2-3% > 1k. The long tail currently drives our cost.

[00:06:35] Owen Patel: Two tactical options: 1) Split routes by expected seqlen so small requests use an aggressive low-latency profile; long sequences use a throughput-optimized kernel (and possibly different model variant). 2) Use early-return/partial-response for certain prompts to cut TTFT.

[00:06:55] Priya Nair: Splitting routes seems easiest operationally for us — route by API endpoint. We'll need SDK changes on our side though.

[00:07:10] Maya Chen: Redwood can provide a sample routing policy and a small SDK snippet. We'll also include a canary template for traffic split tests.

[00:07:26] [00:07:40] Ethan Ruiz: Question — how will quantization affect quality in our prompts? We saw a slight drop in rerank consistency in a few cases during the int8 probe. Samir, you flagged some hallucinations.
[00:07:52] Samir Bhatt: Yeah one or two reranker items changed position in our eval. It's small but noticeable on a handful of prompts.

[00:08:05] Owen Patel: That aligns with known int8 tradeoffs. We can test per-route quant profiles, or use mixed precision on the reranker route to preserve quality. It's more memory but it keeps output stable.

[00:08:20] Priya Nair: For pilot, we want stable user-facing reranks. Mixed precision for that route only sounds good.

[00:08:32] Maya Chen: We'll recommend mixed precision for rerank endpoints, int8 for lower-priority summarization routes.

[00:08:45] [00:09:00] Owen Patel: Back to the TTFT traces — I put three example traces in the drive. Trace A is the cold cache hit with ~42ms first-token cost. Trace B is a warm path at 8ms. Trace C shows the streaming handshake adding ~120ms during a 200-rps microburst.
[00:09:22] Maya Chen: Anyone have questions on those traces?
[00:09:26] Priya Nair: For Trace C, the timeline shows a spike in accept queue latency correlated with a canary deploy. Can we tie churn to that?
[00:09:35] Owen Patel: Likely, yes — when pods are replaced, connection affinity breaks and some in-flight streams land on new workers. We'll propose a short window for draining and a deploy pause for the pilot.

[00:09:48] Samir Bhatt: Would sticky sessions help?
[00:09:52] Owen Patel: Sticky sessions help the KV warmup but are brittle with autoscaling. Better to combine short stickiness with prefix caching plus the fastpath override.

[00:10:06] [00:10:20] Maya Chen: Okay time to decide on the immediate mitigations: 1) fastpath override on runtime, 2) pre-warm streaming acceptor pool, 3) route split for short vs long seqs, 4) mixed precision for rerank route. Any objections?
[00:10:36] Priya Nair: None. Agree.
[00:10:39] Ethan Ruiz: Fine on our end.
[00:10:42] Samir Bhatt: Agree.

[00:10:48] Maya Chen: Good. We'll scope the effort. Owen, how long for the override + pre-warm patch?
[00:10:55] Owen Patel: I can get a vetted config flag and install note today, and the pre-warm patch in two business days. We'll provide a rollback plan.

[00:11:10] Maya Chen: Priya, is legal/security blocking anything for us flipping these runtime flags?
[00:11:17] Priya Nair: No, but we need audit trails and KMS pointers. We have a list of compliance checks, but this is purely an operational change so it's fine. Still want the SOC2 and KMS FAQ.

[00:11:30] Maya Chen: I'll send that.

[00:11:40] [00:12:00] Owen Patel: One more perf note — if we enforce route split, we should avoid model cold-starts when routing long sequences to a different variant. We'll pre-warm the heavy model variant with a low-rate keepalive.
[00:12:14] Samir Bhatt: Ok we'll accept the keepalive cost.

[00:12:25] Maya Chen: On instrumentation — Ethan, you mentioned some metrics were missing during the spike. Which ones?
[00:12:32] Ethan Ruiz: We lack detailed accept queue depth and per-connection handshake timers in our dashboard. We have p50/p95 for token latency but not the subcomponent breakdown in real time.

[00:12:45] Owen Patel: Redwood Console can emit per-route accept latency and handshake histogram. We'll add a dashboard tile for you.

[00:12:55] Maya Chen: We'll also add a microburst-runbook doc describing how to reproduce, what logs to grab, and which perf graphs to include.

[00:13:05] [00:13:25] Priya Nair: Timeline — we want to validate mitigations in the next two weeks. Ideally pushes to staging by end of this week and an ops run against the microburst harness early next week.
[00:13:38] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. To confirm: Owen to push override notes today; pre-warm part by Tue; Samir to run microburst and share logs by Fri; Maya to send SOC2/KMS FAQ by tomorrow.

[00:13:55] Ethan Ruiz: Quick question — any change to billing or usage quotas when we pre-warm idle streams?
[00:14:02] Maya Chen: We'll surface that in the cost estimate — expect a small bump while pre-warm is active. Redwood Optimize can run a cost projection for the pilot config and share a delta.

[00:14:15] Priya Nair: Great. Also, is there a recommended fallback model if the int8 path regresses quality?
[00:14:23] Owen Patel: Yes, we can auto-fallback to a float16 variant for specific routes using routing policy hedging. We'll include that in the rollout plan.

[00:14:36] Maya Chen: Any other blockers?
[00:14:40] Samir Bhatt: Nothing from our end.

[00:14:44] [00:14:55] Maya Chen: Ok quick recap and owners:
- Owen: kernel override doc + pre-warm patch (due 2027-08-16 / 2027-08-17)
- Samir: microburst experiment + logs (due 2027-08-19)
- Maya: SOC2/KMS FAQ and cost delta (due 2027-08-16)
- Redwood: provide route-splitting sample and SDK snippet (due 2027-08-18)

[00:15:20] Priya Nair: We'll schedule the kernel profiling session next week with Owen.

[00:15:28] Owen Patel: Great, I'll bring flamegraphs and a live trace.

[00:15:35] Maya Chen: Anything else before we wrap?
[00:15:38] Ethan Ruiz: One small ask — can Redwood capture per-request model variant in traces? That would help us correlate quality drops.
[00:15:46] Owen Patel: Yes we can add a model_variant tag to the logs and trace IDs.

[00:15:52] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the ticket with the docs and scheduling links.
[00:15:58] Priya Nair: Thanks all.
[00:16:00] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear of KV cache (transcribed as K-V cash), timestamps approximate. Some sentences run-on as recorded in quick talk over details.
